lines.trans: Yuna is great as an emcee—she is the best!

lines.trans: Her public image is way too tarnished lately—she has been unpopular for ages, and even her agency gave up managing her.
You know she is not like that! And if the public dislikes her, we can shape a great persona and make her likable again!
Senior, we are producers—watching an innocent kid get smeared right before our eyes, can we really do nothing for her?
Just because we are producers, do we get to decide everything? Once viewers turn their backs, what power does a producer have?
I told you I will take full responsibility!

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: verb to decide

examples.trans: I decided.
Let's decide.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 비뇨기 계통은 젊었을 때 잘 관리를 해줘야 돼!
examples.trans: You have to take good care of urological health while you are young!
Here the word for 'care, management' is key.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

examples.text: 당연해 그건. 점심 먹어야지. 여기서 군만두 맛있어.
examples.trans: Of course you won't. Let's eat lunch. The fried dumplings here are delicious.
Today's atmosphere is truly natural, of course.

meanings.en: to suffer / be on the receiving end of
meanings.note: Used when someone is the victim or recipient of an undesirable event

examples.trans: My friend got hit in a fender-bender yesterday.
Be careful not to fall victim to voice phishing.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun + object (독박을).

examples.text: 네가 뭘 어떻게 책임을 져! 네 정의감 때문에 프로그램 망가져도 상관없어? 우리가 왜 독박을 뒤집어쓰냐고!
examples.trans: How on earth will you take responsibility?! Does wrecking the show for your sense of justice not matter—why should our team take the fall?!
This point about the sole blame is really important.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used as quotative question (뒤집어쓰냐고!).

examples.text: 네가 뭘 어떻게 책임을 져! 네 정의감 때문에 프로그램 망가져도 상관없어? 우리가 왜 독박을 뒤집어쓰냐고!
examples.trans: How on earth will you take responsibility?! Does wrecking the show for your sense of justice not matter—why should our team take the fall?!
Let us do that (should take the fall) right away.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (등지면).

examples.text: 우리가 피디면 우리가 다 결정할 수 있냐? 시청자 등지면 피디가 무슨 힘이 있니?
examples.trans: Just because we are producers, do we get to decide everything? Once viewers turn their backs, what power does a producer have?
Let us do that (if we alienate) right away.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (만들어주면).

examples.text: 그런 애 아니잖아! 그리고 비호감인 거는 우리가 캐릭터 잘 잡아서 호감으로 만들어주면 되잖아!
examples.trans: You know she is not like that! And if the public dislikes her, we can shape a great persona and make her likable again!
Let us do that (if we rebuild for her) right away.

meanings.note: Used as concessive -어도 (망가져도).

examples.text: 네가 뭘 어떻게 책임을 져! 네 정의감 때문에 프로그램 망가져도 상관없어? 우리가 왜 독박을 뒤집어쓰냐고!
examples.trans: How on earth will you take responsibility?! Does wrecking the show for your sense of justice not matter—why should our team take the fall?!
Let us do that (even if it gets ruined) right away.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (믿고).

examples.text: 신디야, 이제 내가 네 엄마야. 엄마만 믿고 따라오면 돼.
examples.trans: Cindy, from now on I am your mother—just trust Mom and follow me.
Let us do that (trusting and) right away.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
Did you hear about this as disliked?
I was busy today because of as disliked.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (빤히).

examples.text: 형, 우리가 피디인데 애가 아무 죄 없이 당하는 거 빤히 보면서 아무것도 못 해줘요?
examples.trans: Senior, we are producers—watching an innocent kid get smeared right before our eyes, can we really do nothing for her?
I thought it over again (plainly).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 선배님이 얘기하신 게 거짓말이라면 기억을 해도 상관없는 거고,
examples.trans: If what you said was a lie, it should not matter even if he remembers.

meanings.note: Used as noun + genitive (소속사의).

examples.trans: Tell them our Cindy needed rest and is resting comfortably under her agency's thorough protection.

examples.text: 받아 적어. 신디는 소속사의 철저한 보호 아래 놀란 심신을 다스리는 중, 심리적인 충격이 큰 듯.
examples.trans: Write this down: Cindy is calming her shaken mind and body under thorough agency protection, apparently in deep psychological shock.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.

meanings.note: Combines 시청 ('watching and listening') + 자 ('person').

examples.trans: Many viewers like that drama.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Usually followed by a negative verb to mean 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

examples.trans: Nobody is here.
Please give me anything.

examples.text: 뭘 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠으면 아무것도 안 하면 돼요.
examples.trans: If you don't know what to do, you don't have to do anything at all.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

examples.text: 겁도 없이 혼자 있을 때 남자 집에 들어오라고 하는 거 아니야.
examples.trans: You shouldn't fearlessly invite a man inside when you are home alone.

examples.text: 그럼 우리 일 위 후보 없이 방송 가는 거예요?
examples.trans: Then are we airing the broadcast without the first-place contender?

meanings.note: Used as acronym noun + polite copula (MC예요?).

examples.trans: Am I a show host here? Why am I hosting this whole conversation by myself?
This point about am I an emcee is really important.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 요사이

examples.trans: How have you been doing these days?
I have too much work lately.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.

examples.text: 그동안 차갑게만 보이던 내 이미지를 친근하게 바꾸려는 거야.
examples.trans: I am going to change my cold image into something friendly and approachable.

examples.trans: These shoes look like I tried too hard when I am going for an easygoing image.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Her public image is way too tarnished lately—she has been unpopular for ages, and even her agency gave up managing her.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (정의감).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 됐어, 넌 무슨 죄니 중간에 껴서.

I'll leave right now.

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!

examples.trans: I lost rock-paper-scissors and was already filmed carrying them all day.

examples.trans: The three essentials for humans are clothing, food, and shelter, and once you enter the editing room you give up clothing and shelter.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

meanings.note: Used by a younger male to address an older brother or close older male friend/colleague.

examples.trans: Hey, do you have time tonight?
My older brother is an office worker.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 백승찬은 해맑은 데가 있어서 호감일 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Baek Seung-chan has an innocent, sunny side, so viewers might really warm up to him.
Here the word for 'likable' is key.

examples.text: 잊지 않고 꼭 갚아 줄 수 있어야 피디한테 힘이 생겨.
examples.trans: Only when people know you remember and repay every debt does a producer gain power.
